NIGHTSWEEP · 1.8 ALPHA BUILD 2

Forward & return setup

Two workflows for the plant you are working on.

Your deployed fleet: Vecima nodes and AOI active equipment use 204/258 MHz high split. GS7000/GS7K, GainMaker and all other node/amplifier families use 42/54 MHz. This local rule is separate from manufacturer capability. Saved field jobs are preserved for review.

Equipment firstGS7K setupPracticeLocal targetsOEM / thermalACI DSIM42/54 MHz204/258 MHz

Use the local design and exact equipment procedure for targets and adjustments. NightSweep provides guidance and records; the ONX, amplifier controls and operator systems perform the measurements and configuration.

START HERE

Identify the launch and installed equipment

Open Route → Setup. Choose Node output, Amplifier / LE output, or Manual / other output. Record the exact module, split, RF leg, actual markers and launch levels. The selected source feeds the first cable span directly; no artificial gain stage or automatic test-point correction is added.

Open Source setup & manual or Route → Amp / node setup. Select the launch source or a route active. For GainMaker, choose Installed gain control: OEM GainMaker AGC, ACI DSIM, or Manual / thermal control. Then choose its complete Documented setup method and confirm the exact manual, installed detector/pilot, firmware and measurement plane. The read-only Setup frequencies & job levels card shows selected-profile design anchors/levels, separate TX reference/service plan and pilot context; confirm applicability to the selected station. It does not supply measured readings. Continue to the plant-specific sweep workflow below. Reviewed steps are records, not acceptance.

Historical manufacturer-authored guides are labeled. Exact EN9000/RFAM/RPD, Quantum18 LE and Quantum18 BA commissioning guides remain manual-access gaps; obtain the matching guide from the manufacturer. Do not substitute an amplifier guide for another model.

The newest public EN9000 family brief located is September 2026. It is not a commissioning manual. Its ERM3-conditioned RF table and separate ERM3/ERM4 capability must match the installed RPD; test-point coupling remains sourced to May 2024. The 180 W PSU output and 200 W thermal quantities are not typical AC consumption.

For standard GS7000, identify receiver/FCM routing, set the OIB receiver pad for the highest required port, lower shared ports with individual output pads and select the matching path EQs. Conventional LCM Auto Set-Up discovers modules; it is not RF balancing. Intelligent-node LCS Auto Setup is a separate forward OIB procedure after saved targets and enabled Port 1; it does not align return.

AOI HGD/HGBT uses saved downstream profile → downstream Auto → optional downstream Manual → upstream alignment from the last amplifier → ALSC after both paths. The V02102025 original PDF returned HTTP 404; the labeled historical manufacturer-authored mirror is the reviewed reference. Latest-issued applicability still requires manufacturer confirmation. Its upstream Manual instrument procedure is distinct from the local XPERTrak return-sweep method.

NODE LAUNCH

GS7000 / GS7K setup in the app

  1. Open Route → Setup → Node output. Select the exact GS7000 1 GHz or standard 1.2 GHz model, installed split, asset and RF port. Record receiver/transmitter/launch modules, segmentation and actual spectrum. Enter job targets or readings; node selection does not choose launch levels.
  2. Open Source setup & manual, or Route → Amp / node setup and select the source. Current launch setup selectors cover standard 1 GHz and standard 1.2 GHz only. SHO/Fiber Deep, Intelligent and retrofit-RPD documents remain exact-variant references, not added setup selectors; do not borrow their receiver tables.
  3. Under the approved service procedure, verify optical input and receiver attenuation. Set the standard node’s OIB receiver pad for the highest required level in a segment, reduce other shared ports with their output pads, and choose the matching path EQs for tilt. Recheck both markers and affected ports.
  4. Add only uncorrected test-point coupling once. Conventional LCM Auto Set-Up discovers modules, not RF level/tilt balancing. Intelligent LCS forward Auto Setup is a separate procedure and does not align return.
  5. Complete the exact transmitter/EDR/RPD return procedure and your GS7K 42/54 forward/Return Sweepless Sweep workflow. The separate 204/258 forward Sweepless Sweep/XPERTrak return workflow belongs to your Vecima/AOI plant. Save actual settings, readings and evidence; checkmarks alone are not acceptance.

USER-LOCAL DESIGN REFERENCES

Non-high-split levels and return TX reference

ReferenceUser-supplied valueQualification
Forward low31 dBmV at 54 MHzLocal design anchor; verify actual downstream carrier, channel-power convention and station output plane
Forward high43 dBmV at 860 MHzSame design and measurement basis; not a universal equipment limit
Return TX38 dBmVSeparate transmitter reference; verify transmitter, signal-power convention and measurement plane

38 dBmV is a level, not MHz. Return TX channels/frequencies and service/sweep plan have not been supplied; enter the verified operator plan. Keep local forward anchors, the approved installed-detector AGC pilot and the exact manufacturer backoff-test frequency separate. Historical 711 MHz DSIM lookup practice is not a universal pilot setting; no universal OEM pilot is assumed.

Procedure purposeSource frequency reference
Conventional OEM manual backoff445.25 / 547.25 / 870 / 1000 MHz printed columns; system amplifier OL-31156-01 p53 and LE OL-31155-01 pp49–50 use different values. 860 MHz is not a printed column; no automatic rounding to 870 or interpolation.
DSIM-SG Rev H manual backoff3.2 dB at 547 MHz; 4.1 dB at 750 MHz; 4.6 dB at 870 MHz, pp2/10. Separate from OEM charts and pilot selection.
OEM or DSIM AGC pilotActual compatible detector/module and approved live carrier. No universal 303/711 MHz pilot is selected; a factory preset does not approve a plant setting.

54 MHz is outside the LGD 65/86 and all catalog Quantum18 forward bands; use an approved in-band job marker there. OEM thermal setup does not use the manual-backoff chart. Quantum18 HGD/HGBT DS Auto profile frequencies/power are job-specific; ALSC/Auto Align Marker Pilots are information, and exact LE/BA setup-frequency procedures remain missing.

Choose Test → References → Your local non-high-split targets → Local non-high-split: 31 @ 54 / 43 @ 860 · TX 38. After confirmation it changes the selected eligible design profile’s forward anchors and the separate 42 MHz TX reference to 38 dBmV. It preserves measured Route Setup fields and existing records and leaves criteria unapproved. Return ceiling ≥204 MHz or a downstream band excluding 54 MHz blocks this preset; a lower return split alone does not make 54 MHz usable.

Test → Meter setup → 42/54 MHz uses separate Operator return TX reference (dBmV) and Return TX frequencies / service plan fields. Enter the verified plan; no return frequencies are inferred. It is not desired injection, generator output, CMTS/receiver level or a relative-return target, and it adds no 42 MHz generator calculation.

OEM/DSIM practice uses synthetic raw 11/23 dBmV plus one 20 dB remaining addback = 31/43 dBmV at 54/860 MHz. GS7K design carries these anchors and the separate 38 dBmV TX reference while its actual markers/readings/TP correction remain blank. The complete GS7K/GainMaker GaN example uses 54/860 MHz and 31/43 dBmV on 42/54 MHz, with six synthetic originals. The separate Vecima/AOI six-active example stays 261/993 MHz and 34/46 dBmV on 204/258 MHz.

Convert to actual available setup frequencies

The local anchors remain 31 dBmV at 54 MHz / 43 dBmV at 860 MHz. Ranges such as 57–753 MHz or 63–550 MHz do not become new 31/43 anchors. Confirm actual carrier centers and power/measurement convention rather than treating spectrum edges as channels.

Open Test → References → Setup targets at available carriers. Enter Available low/high carrier (MHz), then select Target curve: Square-root frequency · cable law or Linear MHz under the local procedure. Inputs start blank; Fill example 57 / 753 MHz and Fill example 63 / 550 MHz change the draft only. The converter requires 54 ≤ low < high ≤ 860 MHz, compatible non-high-split profile/hardware and compliance with a known entered live-spectrum upper limit. No target is extrapolated; blank live coverage remains unverified. Neither choice establishes an operator-approved tilt shape or installed equipment response. Example pairs fill draft frequencies only; base profile, actual launch readings and records remain unchanged.

Setup-frequency exampleSquare-root estimate low/high (dBmV)Linear-MHz estimate low/high (dBmV)
57 / 753 MHz31.11 / 41.9731.04 / 41.41
63 / 550 MHz31.32 / 39.7931.13 / 38.38

The original 54/860 MHz anchors remain 31/43 dBmV (12 dB rise). The square-root estimated rises over the example ranges are 10.86 and 8.47 dB. Fresh Wolfram evaluation checked these formulas/endpoints, not an installed equalizer or an operator-approved curve.

Full project backups retain the conversion draft. Equipment setup’s Setup frequencies & job levels card separates calculated carrier targets from base anchors. Run-sheet HTML/text/CSV records the frequencies, estimated levels, curve and base reference without claiming measured acceptance or filling measurements.

Compare the calculated frequency-specific targets with actual readings and add only remaining uncompensated TP coupling once. Complete GS7K/GainMaker and focused OEM/DSIM/GS7K practice retain the local 54/860 base design during available-carrier conversion. The separate Vecima/AOI six-active 204/258 example retains its own in-band markers.

GAINMAKER FITTED CONTROL

OEM AGC and manual/thermal setup

Choose the complete Manual backoff → OEM AGC or Thermal setup → OEM AGC branch applicable to the installed station. Manual backoff uses S1 = 2 and the exact station’s temperature/reference-frequency chart before pad/EQ adjustment; thermal setup uses S1 = 1 without adding that manual chart. The system amplifier and LE charts differ.

For the cited conventional 1 GHz GaAs HGD/HGBT/LGD, the pad relationship is corrected MAIN-output pilot dBmV − 34 dB; applicable 1 GHz AGC LE uses corrected output-pilot dBmV − 29 dB. The exact detector and pilot convention must match. No OEM QAM detector-offset bulletin was recovered; the −6 dB distortion-loading convention is not an AGC correction. These relationships are not DSIM pad settings or unresolved GaN instructions.

Follow the selected procedure through S1 = 3, match AGC GAIN to the setup reading and verify output after settling between switch changes. The cited OEM procedure gives no universal settling timer. Apply raw −20 dB coupling once only if the meter has not already corrected it.

Thermal-only methods distinguish amplifier-only compensation (S1 = 1) from amplifier-plus-coax compensation (S1 = 3), following the matching warm/cold procedure. The cold-equipment procedure is not a blanket −1 dB target. A manual LE has no Bode network and S1 has no operating-mode effect. Exact installed GaN HGD I&O/control remains a documentation hold.

Use only current equipment. Two UBT RF outputs and three UBT power presets remain readable for legacy saved jobs but are absent from new equipment selection/workflows. HGBT and passive unbalanced three-way outputs remain current.

GAINMAKER CONTROL OPTION

Optional ACI DSIM setup and pilot codes

Identify the installed RF module, DSIM variant, firmware and applicable procedure revision. DSIM-SG, DSIM-A and conventional GainMaker AGC are separate control methods. Record the approved pilot type, channel and center frequency.

Follow the matching interface procedure

Equipment setup provides eight ordered SG Rev G/H physical-controller steps, including manual preparation, the documented 0 dB pad, solid-blue MGC, temperature preparation, 9/18/27 dB thermal-fallback factor, pilot alignment and final output/mode verification. The physical-controller temperature table is separate from ACI mobile-app Rev B AGC Prep. In the app, minus decreases attenuation for cold preparation and plus increases it for hot preparation; raw attenuation-position counts are not dB. Follow the complete matching interface guide.

Use the supplied pilot-code lookup

Open Route → Amp / node setup, select the GainMaker station and DSIM variant, then match channel, Analog/Digital type and MHz in the pilot-code lookup. Review the source and any exception; use Copy only for an eligible exact result and paste it into ACI’s controller/app. Preserve every character. The source is the user-supplied ACI iPhone/iPad Pilot Channel Code Guide, Rev A, pp 2–5: 86 literal rows, channels 52–94 and 100–142. These are historical table entries, not a universal supervisor password, hardware validation or firmware/app compatibility approval.

Digital channelFrequencyExact source code
110711 MHz@@?<A
88609 MHzGG<A

No supplied rows cover channels 95–99 or 303 MHz, so no codes are fabricated. OFDM PLC compatibility is not established by the QAM pilot table.

Channel 100 source exception: the row prints analog 649.25 MHz / HD<@ and digital 651 MHz / HD<A. The row is flagged and copying is blocked while unresolved. Confirm the original source and intended pilot before use; no replacement value is invented.

Match the setup revision before choosing pads

DSIM-SG Rev E, October 3, 2015, pp 2 and 10, specifies 10 dB AGC pad for LE and 6 dB for the applicable HGD. Rev H, April 8, 2021, specifies 0 dB. Apply the complete matching procedure for the installed module/revision; do not combine settings across revisions.

The historical DSIM-A Rev T guide, December 14, 2017, is an additional reference. It does not establish applicability to the later 1218 MHz DSIM-A-MDL-1201 variant; that variant’s exact procedure must be confirmed. The SG guide and later DSIM datasheet also conflict on SG supply-voltage thresholds. Pilot-code availability does not resolve those equipment questions.

  • ACI DSIM-SG guide · Rev H · April 8, 2021
  • Historical ACI DSIM-A guide · Rev T · December 14, 2017
  • ACI DSIM app guide · Rev B · March 24, 2021 · p11

Confirm the actual live pilot and alignment result in the applicable ACI hardware/app and approved local workflow. NightSweep does not connect to DSIM or establish acceptance from a code lookup. Keep private operator passwords out of notes and backups.

LEGACY

42/54 MHz · Forward and return sweepless

Live-service workflow for the ONX-630: forward Sweepless Sweep and DOCSIS Reverse Sweepless Sweep. Menu labels follow the VIAVI v5.5 guide; installed firmware may differ. All levels and acceptance limits come from the local design.

  1. Identify the 42 MHz system

    Record node, leg, station, exact amplifier model and installed 42/54 MHz diplex configuration. Confirm the ONX has the required reverse-sweepless option and a compatible DOCSIS RF module.

    Enter the actual downstream operating band, upstream carrier coverage, approved reference location and design targets. Keep the 42 MHz job separate from the 204 MHz profile; do not inherit injection or receiver targets from another plant.

  2. Connect and configure forward sweepless

    Open CATV Network → Sweepless Sweep. Stop → Configure → Configure Test Point. Copy a locked template, name it for the connection, enter the verified forward correction, then Done/Start. These templates apply to expert tests, not ordinary CATV tests.

    Record probe, lead, port and compensation already applied. Add each loss once. Confirm the installed split and actual downstream carriers; the split edge is not automatically a usable marker.

  3. Save the forward baseline

    At the approved reference location, verify design output level and tilt before saving. Use Stop → Configure → Save Test/Reference; give it a node/port/location name and select Set as Reference. Record the forward tilt compensation and its low/high anchor frequencies.

    Keep the original baseline. A trace normalized against itself can look flat while its absolute launch level is wrong.

  4. Check the forward cascade

    Compare each downstream station with the appropriate saved baseline, using consistent carrier selections and correction settings. Record actual levels, marker frequencies, tilt and response irregularities. Complete forward setup using the exact equipment procedure and design targets before return alignment.

    Attach the trace and downstream quality measurements. The downstream QAM/OFDM screens document forward performance; they cannot establish return gain or return acceptance.

  5. Start DOCSIS reverse sweepless

    Select Reverse Sweepless Sweep through Sweep Mode where offered. Stop → Configure: select the site DOCSIS Service Plan and correct test-point template, including separate forward and reverse compensation. Start and wait for DOCSIS Connected.

    This uses DOCSIS operation and adds no sweep pulses. It requires live service and measures occupied upstream spectrum only. If DOCSIS cannot connect, mark the return test incomplete and troubleshoot the connection; do not substitute a passing calculation.

  6. Set a consistent return display basis

    Record Ref BW and keep it consistent: Modem Default, 1.7 MHz or 6.4 MHz. Modem Default uses each SC-QAM channel bandwidth and 1.7 MHz for OFDMA. Changing between 1.7 and 6.4 MHz changes normalized power by 6 dB.

    Display → Sweep View Type offers Detailed or 1.7 MHz; this is a separate setting. Record actual tested channels, not just a nominal 5–42 MHz label.

  7. Establish and retain the return reference

    Verify the reference location against the approved design before saving. Absolute is the estimated adjusted response at the CMTS/RPHY; Referenced shows change from the saved location. Neither is automatically a direct RF reading at the node test point.

    Save a named reference with Set as Reference, or use Configure → Choose Reference. Record its node/port, service plan, Ref BW and corrections. Do not replace the baseline merely to remove an unfavorable trace.

  8. Balance the verified legacy amplifier cascade

    For the cited conventional GainMaker procedure, establish the reverse optical link first, then work from the node toward successive amplifiers and branches. Check the exact station manual before changing pads.

    The amplifier reverse output EQ controls received tilt; the reverse output pad controls level. More output pad reduces received level. Preserve design reverse input pads unless the applicable procedure calls for a temporary change, and restore them afterward. Node optical-drive settings have their own procedure.

  9. Evaluate each occupied segment

    Wait for DOCSIS results to settle after a change. Review referenced A/B levels and Min/Max Δ against the locally approved criteria. Negative referenced response indicates relative loss; positive indicates relative gain.

    Track absolute transmit/receive information as well as the referenced shape. Do not use a sweepless CMTS estimate as a CW receiver target in a pad calculator. Gaps outside active channels remain untested; further testing needs the operator-approved method.

  10. Verify, save and close out

    Save separate before/after traces and the unchanged baseline identity. Record equipment/port, settings changed, measured coverage, targets, correction basis, result time and unresolved faults. Check ingress and DOCSIS service performance as additional evidence.

    Use Measured / Incomplete / Needs review until the required evidence and operator limits are available. Mark unmeasured frequencies explicitly. Export the job with its original files for supervisor review.

HIGH SPLIT

204/258 MHz · Forward sweepless and XPERTrak return sweep

High-split workflow using forward Sweepless Sweep and active return sweep through the operator’s XPERTrak-supported deployment. NightSweep records and guides the work; it does not configure the ONX, RPD or XPERTrak.

  1. Identify the high-split path

    Record node/RPD identity, upstream port or segment, station/leg, exact amplifier and installed 204/258 MHz configuration. Confirm meter hardware, options and firmware support the required band and test mode.

    Enter the actual test limits and reference plane. A 204 MHz split does not define the sweep-plan endpoints, occupied channels or receiver target. Verify the route and return port paths independently of forward losses.

  2. Connect and configure forward sweepless

    Open CATV Network → Sweepless Sweep. Stop → Configure → Configure Test Point. Copy a locked template, name it for the connection, enter the verified forward correction, then Done/Start. These templates apply to expert tests, not ordinary CATV tests.

    Record probe, lead, port and compensation already applied. Add each loss once. Confirm the installed split and actual downstream carriers; the split edge is not automatically a usable marker.

  3. Save the forward baseline

    At the approved reference location, verify design output level and tilt before saving. Use Stop → Configure → Save Test/Reference; give it a node/port/location name and select Set as Reference. Record the forward tilt compensation and its low/high anchor frequencies.

    Keep the original baseline. A trace normalized against itself can look flat while its absolute launch level is wrong.

  4. Check the forward cascade

    Compare each downstream station with the appropriate saved baseline, using consistent carrier selections and correction settings. Record actual levels, marker frequencies, tilt and response irregularities. Complete forward setup using the exact equipment procedure and design targets before return alignment.

    Attach the trace and downstream quality measurements. The downstream QAM/OFDM screens document forward performance; they cannot establish return gain or return acceptance.

  5. Confirm XPERTrak sweep readiness

    Use the approved operator procedure to confirm the correct node/RPD upstream port, sweep-plan identity and enabled sweep service. For supported R-PHY deployments, the RPD provides the receiver and downstream telemetry, coordinated by XPERTrak RCI.

    Record the approved telemetry frequencies, user mode, sweep coverage and test levels. Exact portal controls vary by deployment; this guide does not supply guessed clicks. Field View spectrum monitoring is distinct from Reverse Sweep.

  6. Configure the meter for active return sweep

    Open Reverse Sweep. In Configure, match the operator’s telemetry and user-mode settings. Select the connection’s test-point template and correct single/dual-port arrangement; verify forward and reverse paths match that wiring.

    Confirm usable telemetry and a fresh response from the intended receiver before alignment. If absent, resolve node/port selection, enabled service, meter mode and physical connection before changing plant settings.

  7. Confirm injection and receiver conventions

    Keep desired network-plane injection, coupling/lead loss and raw generator output distinct. The ONX template combines Reverse Sweep Injection with Reverse TPC; do not add the same coupling loss again. Check the installed meter’s total output limit.

    Enter the receiver target with its exact RF/digital reference plane and measurement basis. Previously discussed 31 dBmV injection and −8 dBmV receive are unconfirmed site examples, not defaults. Sweeping through occupied OFDMA requires the operator’s approved plan and settings.

  8. Save the approved active-sweep reference

    At the approved baseline location, confirm absolute level and response meet the design. Save a named test/reference; retain node/port, telemetry, injection, correction and plan details. At later locations select the matching reference.

    Record both absolute and referenced evidence. Normalizing a trace does not prove correct optical/RPD drive or absolute gain. Keep the same comparison basis and identify any plan changes before interpreting differences.

  9. Apply the sequence for the exact amplifier

    Quantum18 SA HGD/HGBT: the cited AOI guide starts upstream alignment at the last amplifier after the cascade’s downstream setup is complete. For its Auto mode, use Upstream → Start Auto in the AOI interface, then review the completion result and Save/Revert decision. Continue according to that model’s procedure.

    This is distinct from manual GainMaker node-outward balancing. Do not apply SA auto-alignment instructions to LE, BA, another hardware revision or manual sweep adjustment without its matching procedure. Record how each station was aligned, then verify with return sweep.

  10. Verify the return path and investigate exceptions

    Compare fresh traces at the required stations/branches with the approved reference. Record level, tilt, response deviations and actual coverage. Use the exact amplifier’s gain/slope controls or pad/EQ procedure; do not infer settings from its forward gain specification.

    Use XPERTrak spectrum and DOCSIS quality checks to investigate ingress, intermittent noise or service issues that a flat sweep may miss. Preserve unresolved exceptions and their locations.

  11. Verify, save and close out

    Save separate before/after traces and the unchanged baseline identity. Record equipment/port, settings changed, measured coverage, targets, correction basis, result time and unresolved faults. Check ingress and DOCSIS service performance as additional evidence.

    Use Measured / Incomplete / Needs review until the required evidence and operator limits are available. Mark unmeasured frequencies explicitly. Export the job with its original files for supervisor review.
